run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T00:54:34Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by frontend-proxy's own error spans: its 'ingress' spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR (1,349.8 error spans vs 17,729.9 UNSET over 23:54:34–01:09:50Z), and the error rate jumps from 0 at 00:53:34Z to ~180 errors per 2m from 00:54:34Z onward. The proxy's 5xx are 15,000 ms 'UT response_timeout' 504s waiting on its frontend upstream, and its 500s come from POST /api/checkout. Traces show the checkout failure text exactly: checkout's PlaceOrder fails with gRPC 13 'failed to prepare order: failed to get product #…' because checkout's oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct calls fail with gRPC 14 'error reading from server: read tcp 100.96.4.114:59432->100.64.188.136:8080: read: connection reset by peer'; 100.64.188.136:8080 is the product-catalog Service ClusterIP. Chaos-control events in namespace chaos-mesh show a Schedule named otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay spawning NetworkChaos experiments every minute from 00:52:33Z, each 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9' and recovered ~55 s later. product-catalog's pod is Running with 0 restarts and its logs read normally until 00:59:47Z, and the app-level fault-injection flags in flagd-config are all 'off', so the evidence points to an injected network fault on the product-catalog pod rather than a crash or an application flag. Because the chaos Schedule/NetworkChaos objects themselves are not readable with the permitted kinds (the declared delay, duration and change time are unverified, and only events tie the fault to the errors), the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own spans carry errors: over 23:54:34–01:09:50Z its span 'ingress' has 1,349.77 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans against 17,729.97 STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and 'router frontend egress' has 21.34 error spans against 19,057.38 UNSET.

frontend-proxy ingress error spans rise from 0 in the 5m bucket ending 00:49:34Z (4.44) to 151.1 (00:54:34Z), 580.0 (00:59:34Z) and 489.6 (01:04:34Z), while ingress UNSET spans fall from ~3,023–3,195 per 5m to 476.7 and 369.3 per 5m.
At 1-minute resolution the frontend-proxy error increase is 0 through the point at 00:53:34Z and 181.33 at 00:54:34Z, staying near 165–215 per 2m through the last point at 01:03:34Z.

The failing frontend-proxy spans are 'ingress' spans with status error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR and duration ~15,000,000 µs (15.0 s), each having a 'router frontend egress' child of the same duration; one 500 ingress span also appears.

frontend-proxy container logs record '504 UT response_timeout' with the upstream marked 'frontend' and a duration of 15000 ms for GET /api/products/*, GET /api/recommendations and POST /api/checkout (e.g. 01:00:33–01:00:39Z).

checkout spans show the exact dependency error: oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct client spans are error=true with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and otel.status_description 'error reading from server: read tcp 100.96.4.114:59432->100.64.188.136:8080: read: connection reset by peer', with durations up to 42,607,159 µs, and the parent oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans fail with rpc.grpc.status_code=13 and 'failed to prepare order: failed to get product #"6E92ZMYYFZ"'.

frontend spans on the same traces fail with http.status_code=500 on POST /api/checkout and 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' (exception.message '13 INTERNAL: failed to prepare order: failed to get product #…') and on grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder with rpc.grpc.status_code=13.
The Service product-catalog has ClusterIP 100.64.188.136 on port 8080 (targetPort 8080), which is the exact destination address in the 'connection reset by peer' error.

Pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 (labels app.kubernetes.io/name=product-catalog, pod-template-hash=7c7f8b68dc, podIP 100.96.4.247, node i-0b2137ceca968ac10) is Running, Ready, started 2026-11-18T00:16:41Z with restartCount 0.

The newest 200 product-catalog container log lines returned for 00:44:34–01:09:50Z (spanning 00:52:32–00:59:47Z) contain only normal request/serving lines 'Product Found' and periodic 'Reloading Product Catalog...' / 'Loaded 10 products'; no crash or error line appears among them and the container has no previous instance.

Chaos Mesh events in namespace chaos-mesh: the Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay spawned a new NetworkChaos every minute from 00:52:33Z (jj42n) through 01:00:33Z (hcwrz); each shows 'Experiment has started', 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9', then 'Time up according to the duration' and 'Successfully recover chaos for otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9' about 55 seconds later.

product-catalog's own span volume collapses across the incident: oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct goes 2,110 (5m ending 00:54:34Z) → 98.89 (00:59:34Z) → 0 (01:04:34Z), ListProducts 174.4 → 0, and checkout PlaceOrder/GetProduct and frontend GetProduct/product-page spans drop to 0 or near 0 in the same windows.
Error spans by service over 23:54:34–01:09:50Z: frontend-proxy 1,371.1, frontend 282.5, recommendation 3.05, ad 2.04, fraud-detection 1.02, accounting/cart/payment 0.
fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-n7vmf has restartCount 2 with lastState.terminated reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-18T00:48:48Z, and the container restarted at 00:48:49Z.

The flagd-config ConfigMap's demo.flagd.json fault-injection flags relevant to this path (productCatalogFailure, adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, imageSlowLoad, recommendationCacheFailure) all have defaultVariant 'off' in the object read at query time.

The network fault injected by Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay onto pod otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 disrupted traffic to the product-catalog Service (100.64.188.136:8080), producing the connection resets and long hangs on GetProduct; that propagated as checkout PlaceOrder gRPC 13, frontend POST /api/checkout 500s, and finally frontend-proxy 15 s 504 timeouts that sustain the RequestErrorRate alert. The onset (first chaos Applied 00:52:33Z, errors first non-zero in the 00:52:34–00:54:34Z bucket) is consistent, but the experiment's declared delay parameters were not readable.

The near-zero product-catalog/checkout span counts in the last sampled windows (ending 00:59:34Z and 01:04:34Z) may partly reflect requests still in flight or span-export delay under the injected network disruption rather than a full outage of product-catalog; the product-catalog pod itself stayed Running and its log ingestion lagged (newest line 00:59:47Z).

product-catalog was not crashed or restarted during the window: its pod is Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and no previous container instance, so the connection resets cannot be attributed to a restarted or killed product-catalog process.

The application-level fault-injection flags in flagd-config are all 'off', so no productCatalogFailure/adFailure/cartFailure/paymentFailure/imageSlowLoad setting was seen enabled as an alternative fault source (config read at query time, not at incident time).

fraud-detection's OOMKill (exit 137 at 00:48:48Z, restart 00:48:49Z) is rejected as the cause of the frontend-proxy error alert: the failing operations are checkout's ProductCatalogService/GetProduct calls, fraud-detection carries only 1.02 error spans over 75m, and no fraud-detection span appears in the failing checkout traces.
A product-catalog process crash/OOM as the mechanism is rejected: that pod shows Running/Ready, restartCount 0, no previous container instance and only normal 'Product Found' log lines.

Have a human read the Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay and the NetworkChaos objects it creates (kind and spec are not readable with the permitted resource kinds) to confirm the delay/latency, jitter, duration and creation time, and decide whether this recurring one-minute experiment on pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 should be paused.

Verify the RequestErrorRate rule's exact expression/metric (the rule was not returned by the rules query) so the alert's reported value 1.4222 can be reconciled with the trace-derived frontend-proxy error rate.

gaps: The chaos Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay and its NetworkChaos children could not be read as objects (kinds schedule/networkchaos are not in the permitted kind list), so the declared fault (delay value, jitter, duration, direction) and the time the setting was created/changed are unverified; only chaos-mesh events evidence the fault.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule was not found by the rules query (rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no data), so the alert's own expression and its 'current: 1.4222' value could not be tied to a specific metric.
The rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count metric returned no data in the window, so gRPC status codes per client/service could not be cross-checked from that metric.
product-catalog produced no error spans of its own during the window (its span counts fell to 0), so its server-side failure mode is unobserved; the failure evidence sits on callers' client spans.

Log ingestion lags the query time: product-catalog's newest readable line is 00:59:47Z and frontend-proxy's newest readable line is 01:00:54Z although the query window ends 01:09:50Z, so product-catalog behaviour in roughly the last 10 minutes of the window is unknown.
Chaos-mesh events only extend to 01:00:33Z in the returned data, so whether the Schedule kept spawning NetworkChaos experiments after that is unknown.
The change-history integration is not available in this Run, so no deployment/configuration change timeline could be checked alongside the chaos schedule.
next_steps: Inspect the Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay spec (and one of its NetworkChaos objects) to confirm the injected delay parameters and creation time.
Determine whether the recurring product-catalog network-delay experiment is an intentional fault-injection test and, if not, pause/remove the Schedule.
Confirm the RequestErrorRate rule definition and metric so the alert value can be validated against the trace-based error rate.
Re-read product-catalog logs after log ingestion catches up past 01:00Z to confirm whether any application-level errors accompanied the network disruption.
